$comment: Decisions about single named items in the coverage queue, read by tools/coverage.mjs. A skip leaves `--queue` for good and says why. A note stays in the queue and hands its text to whoever writes the card, as `reviewNote`. Matching is exact and case-insensitive on the queue name, or on the sanskrit name for asanas, never fuzzy. Started 2026-09-12, when 19 of the top 25 queue items were names earlier passes had already decided against and were re-reading every twelve hours. Every reason is written here in our own words: the free-exercise-db reference is vendored as names only, on purpose (see the licensing note at the top of coverage.mjs), and nothing in this file copies its text.

entries.name: Runner's Stretch
entries.reason: Single-source identification only, and the source contradicts the vendored muscle tag: the one description found (zing.coach) is a plank-to-lunge dynamic hip-flexor stretch (back knee lowered to the floor), but free-exercise-db tags this entry's primary muscle as hamstrings, not hip flexors/quads. That mismatch, plus the pose it describes already existing here as the already-shipped 'Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch', means writing it risks either a duplicate or a wrong muscle tag. Skipped rather than guessed.

entries.name: Seated Barbell Military Press
entries.reason: The already-shipped 'Seated Barbell Shoulder Press' under free-exercise-db's 'military press' branding for the same lift. Confirmed against four independent sources (workoutlabs, jefit, exrx, opafit): same setup (bench with back support, barbell racked at shoulder height, overhand grip just outside shoulder width, pressed straight overhead), same muscles, same description down to 'the backrest offers light support, not 100% of your weight.' Only the name differs ('military' vs 'shoulder' press is the same movement in free-weight terminology).

entries.name: Seated Bent-Over Rear Delt Raise
entries.reason: The already-shipped 'Seated Dumbbell Rear-Delt Fly': sit on the edge of a bench, hinge forward so the chest nears the thighs, raise the dumbbells out to the sides. 'Rear delt raise' and 'rear-delt fly' are the same movement under two common names, and the shipped card's description matches this queue item's implied setup word for word in substance.

entries.name: Seated Calf Stretch
entries.reason: The already-shipped 'Seated Forward Fold' (yoga-seated-forward-fold): sit with both legs straight out, hinge forward from the hips, hold the shins/ankles/feet. Confirmed against ACE Fitness's description of 'Seated Calf Stretch' (legs extended, reach for feet, hold) -- same pose, same fold; free-exercise-db just tags it for calves (via ankle dorsiflexion at the stretch's end range) where the shipped card tags it for hamstrings. The shipped card's secondaryMuscles already lists Calves.

entries.name: Pullups
entries.reason: The already-shipped 'Pull-Up' under free-exercise-db's unhyphenated spelling. isCovered() missed it because 'pullups' and 'pull-up' tokenize to different word sets (one word vs. two), not because the movement differs -- same grip, same bar, same muscles.

entries.name: Pushups
entries.reason: The already-shipped 'Push-Up' under free-exercise-db's unhyphenated spelling, same tokenization gap as the 'Pullups' skip above.

entries.name: Pushups (Close and Wide Hand Positions)
entries.reason: Names no single movement -- it is free-exercise-db's reference to a comparison of two hand placements already shipped as their own cards ('Diamond Push-Up' for close, 'Wide Push-Up' for wide). A card would have to either duplicate both or arbitrarily pick one.

entries.name: Prone Manual Hamstring
entries.reason: A clinician- or partner-applied manual-resistance hamstring curl (confirmed against PT rehab sources: resistance is applied by hand at the ankle, not by a load). free-exercise-db lists its equipment as null and coverage.mjs remaps that to bodyweight, but there is no solo bodyweight version of 'manual resistance' -- it needs a second person by definition, which this solo-use app does not fit.

entries.name: One-Arm Open Palm Kettlebell Clean
entries.reason: A second free-exercise-db entry for the same coaching drill as the already-skipped 'Open Palm Kettlebell Clean' (2026-10-04), just carrying a redundant 'One-Arm' prefix -- the shipped 'Kettlebell Clean' is already a single-bell, one-arm lift by definition, so neither 'One-Arm' nor the open-palm grip cue changes the movement, load, or muscles worked. Exact-name matching means the earlier skip did not suppress this queue entry; recorded under its own exact name so it does not re-queue.

entries.name: One-Arm Side Laterals
entries.reason: Same movement and same conclusion as the already-skipped 'Side Lateral Raise' (written 2026-10-04 as 'One-Arm Dumbbell Lateral Raise'): the shipped bilateral 'Dumbbell Lateral Raise' already covers it, since nothing about grip, path or stabilizer demand changes when a lateral raise is done one arm at a time. A different free-exercise-db name for the same already-decided case; recorded under its own exact name so it does not re-queue.

entries.name: Overhead Slam
entries.reason: Checked by hand before writing: this is the already-shipped 'Medicine Ball Slam' (id medicine-ball-slam-conditioning) under a shorter name. That card's own description is 'reach it overhead, then forcefully slam it straight down into the floor' -- the identical movement free-exercise-db lists as 'Overhead Slam'. isCovered() would likely read 'overhead' (a DISCRIMINATING word absent from the shipped name) as divergence, which is why it reached the queue uncaught rather than why it is actually a duplicate.

entries.name: Astavakrasana
entries.reason: Eight-angle pose is an advanced arm balance with the whole body held off bent arms. Described even slightly wrong, the hand or leg placement is a real fall or joint-load risk.

entries.name: Kaundinyasana
entries.reason: An advanced arm balance with the legs extended off the arms, carrying the same fall and wrist-load risk as Astavakrasana if the placement is described even slightly wrong.

entries.name: Durvasasana
entries.reason: A standing pose with one leg taken behind the head: an advanced bind with real hip, knee and lower-back strain risk for anyone learning it from a card.

entries.name: Gorakshasana
entries.reason: Two materially different techniques circulate under this name (soles together sitting on the heels, versus the classical ankle lock) and the reference does not say which one it means.

entries.name: Matsyendrasana
entries.reason: Full lord of the fishes forces one foot into half-lotus against the opposite hip, a well-documented way to injure a knee. The deck already carries the safer half version as yoga-seated-spinal-twist.

entries.name: Marichyasana
entries.reason: Names a family of four poses (A to D) that differ materially, some adding a bind with an arm wrapped behind the back, and the reference does not say which. A wrong bind description is a real strain risk.
entries.by: 2026-09-09 morning Bellows pass; confirmed in review 2026-09-12

entries.name: Adductor/Groin
entries.reason: The movement under this name is a partner-resisted groin stretch: someone else holds your legs and pushes them apart. FitFlexr is used alone. Earlier passes skipped it as an unclear name; needing a second person is the real reason.

entries.name: Band Hip Adductions
entries.reason: The reference contradicts itself: the name says adduction (leg drawn in toward the body) while the movement lifts the leg out to the side, which is abduction. The schema also has no hip-adduction pattern, so this needs a schema decision before it can be a card.

entries.name: Alternate Leg Diagonal Bound
entries.reason: The same skater-style bound as the shipped Lateral Bound, travelling diagonally forward instead of straight sideways. Not different enough to earn its own card.

entries.name: Bench Jump
entries.reason: Clearing a full-height bench in one jump means landing from above it, the landing the shipped Box Jump Over card deliberately avoids by stepping down to protect knees and Achilles. A 2026-09-11 card under this name described fast sideways hops over a bench instead, and was dropped in review.

entries.name: Barbell Curls Lying Against An Incline
entries.reason: A curl lying face-down on an incline bench with a straight bar, which is a barbell spider curl. Same target and audience as the shipped Spider Dumbbell Curl and awkward with a straight bar; a pass reached the same conclusion about a barbell spider curl on 2026-09-12.

entries.name: Alternating Deltoid Raise
entries.reason: Not ambiguous. With a dumbbell in each hand the reps alternate: one front raise to shoulder height, then one side raise to shoulder height, and repeat. Earlier passes skipped it believing the name did not say which raise; it is both, in turn.

entries.name: Anti-Gravity Press
entries.reason: A light shoulder drill, not an overhead press. Lying face-down on an incline bench, the bar starts close to your chest and is pressed straight out in front of your head, arms travelling parallel to the floor, then brought back in.

entries.name: Barbell Incline Shoulder Raise
entries.reason: Lying back on an incline bench with the bar held straight up at arm's length, raise it a few inches using only your shoulder blades, arms staying straight, then lower. A serratus drill; it must not be written as a press.

entries.name: Bent Over One-Arm Long Bar Row
entries.reason: A one-arm landmine row: one end of a barbell anchored in a corner or landmine, plates on the other end, rowed one-handed while the other hand rests on your knee. The two-handed version is the shipped T-Bar Row. If the card gets a different title, give it this name as an alias or coverage keeps queueing it.

entries.name: Barbell Step Ups
entries.reason: Not a duplicate. Step-ups already ship as separate box, dumbbell and kettlebell cards; this is the version with a barbell across the upper back, equipment barbell and box. A 2026-09-12 pass judged it too close to Box Step-Up.

entries.name: Barbell Shoulder Press
entries.reason: Not a duplicate of the shipped Barbell Overhead Press, which is standing. The movement under this name is seated on a bench with back support, equipment barbell and bench, the way dumbbell presses already ship as separate seated and standing cards. Title it Seated Barbell Shoulder Press and keep this name as an alias.

entries.name: Bent Press
entries.reason: An expert-level kettlebell lift whose whole point is that the arm barely moves and the body presses itself out from under the bell via a sideways hip/lat hinge -- the opposite of a normal press. A description that reads as 'press overhead while leaning to the side' would teach the wrong pattern under a loaded, twisted spine, and that residual uncertainty about the exact hip/lat sequencing is enough on its own to skip a spinal-loading lift.

entries.name: Bodyweight Flyes
entries.reason: The reference tags this with e-z curl bar equipment, but a flye is defined by each arm independently arcing outward -- both hands fixed to one bar cannot do that motion, so the name and the equipment contradict each other. Free-exercise-db elsewhere uses this name for a TRX/strap flye, which is a different, plausible movement; without knowing which one this record means, writing either is a guess.

entries.name: Butt Lift (Bridge)
entries.reason: The bodyweight bridge under this name is the shipped Glute Bridge: lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat, drive the hips up. No distinguishing detail in the reference separates it from the shipped card.

entries.name: Butterfly
entries.reason: The standard alternate name for the machine chest fly, already shipped as Pec Deck Fly (equipment: machine, same seated-arms-wide-squeeze-together movement).

entries.name: Butt-Ups
entries.reason: Not confident of the exact setup from the name alone -- this could be a kneeling hip-thrust ab drill or something closer to the shipped Glute Bridge/Reverse Crunch family, and the reference gives no instructions to check against. A wrong ab card is worse than a missing one.

entries.name: Cable Incline Pushdown
entries.reason: The reference tags this as a lats exercise, but 'pushdown' as a name is otherwise only used here for triceps cable work. Not confident enough of the incline-bench setup that turns a pushdown into a lat movement to write it without guessing.

entries.name: Cable Iron Cross
entries.reason: A wide-arm cable chest movement pulled in toward center is already covered by the shipped Cable Chest Fly and High/Low Cable Crossover. Not confident the 'iron cross' starting position (arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height, rather than a slight bend) is different enough to earn its own card rather than guessing at a distinction that isn't real.

entries.name: Cable Judo Flip
entries.reason: A diagonal rotational cable pull for the obliques reads as the same movement as the shipped Cable Woodchopper. Not confident there's a real distinguishing detail behind the name rather than a second title for the same chop.

entries.name: Cable Lying Triceps Extension
entries.reason: Lying on a bench facing away from a low pulley, gripping a rope or bar behind the head and extending overhead, reads as the same setup and movement as the just-shipped Cable Incline Triceps Extension — only the bench angle differs, which is not a distinct exercise.

entries.name: Cable Rope Rear-Delt Rows
entries.reason: A rope pulled toward the face/upper chest with elbows flared and high, targeting the rear delts and upper back, is the shipped Cable Face Pull. Not confident there's a real distinguishing pull path (to the chest with elbows back, rather than to the face with elbows up) behind the name rather than a second title for the same pull.

entries.name: Calf Stretch Hands Against Wall
entries.reason: Word-for-word the shipped Standing Calf Stretch (tf-standing-calf-stretch): 'both hands on it', one foot back, heel pressed into the floor, leg straight. No distinguishing detail in the reference separates it from the shipped card.

entries.name: Calf-Machine Shoulder Shrug
entries.reason: Uses a standing calf-raise machine's shoulder pads to shrug instead of raise the heels. Standing calf machines are not one standardized geometry (platform height, pad angle, knee-lock position vary by brand), and F10's lesson is exactly this: a confidently wrong setup description on unfamiliar equipment is worse than no card. Cable Shrug and the existing Dumbbell/Barbell Shrug already cover the movement pattern.

entries.name: Cat Stretch
entries.reason: The reference gives name and equipment only (bodyweight, stretching, lower back). The shipped Cat-Cow (yoga-cat-cow) is the same hands-and-knees spine-rounding movement; nothing in the reference distinguishes a standalone 'Cat Stretch' from the cat half of that pose.

entries.name: Chair Squat
entries.reason: Tagged equipment 'machine' in the reference, but the name describes a bodyweight sit-to-a-chair squat with no machine involved. That mismatch between name and equipment is the exact class of error F10 warns about — writing a setup for whichever reading is wrong would ship a confidently incorrect card.

entries.name: Chest Push (multiple response)
entries.reason: A medicine-ball plyometric combine drill. The reference gives no instructions, and 'multiple response' vs 'single response' vs '3 point stance' vs 'run release' are four variants of the same throw distinguished only by stance and rep scheme — details easy to conflate from the name alone, and this app has no rebounder/wall-toss equipment concept to anchor which setup is meant.

entries.name: Chest Push (single response)
entries.reason: Same medicine-ball chest-push family as 'Chest Push (multiple response)' — see that entry. Not confident which setup detail (wall vs partner, stance) separates it from the other three variants.

entries.name: Chest Push from 3 point stance
entries.reason: Same medicine-ball chest-push family as 'Chest Push (multiple response)' — see that entry. Not confident which setup detail separates it from the other three variants.

entries.name: Chest Push with Run Release
entries.reason: Same medicine-ball chest-push family as 'Chest Push (multiple response)' — see that entry. Not confident which setup detail separates it from the other three variants.

entries.name: Clean
entries.reason: Barbell, floor-to-shoulders, the shipped Barbell Clean (barbell-clean-conditioning) already is this movement under a fuller name.

entries.name: Clean from Blocks
entries.reason: A full clean, catch and all, starting with the bar on elevated blocks instead of the floor. The catch is the hardest part of a clean to describe correctly (Clean and Jerk's own catch needed a correction in the 2026-09-14 review), and 'blocks' commonly means either below-knee or above-knee height with no way to tell which this name intends. Not confident enough to write either detail.

entries.name: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Curl with Band
entries.reason: A close-grip EZ-bar curl with a resistance band looped around the bar ends and anchored underfoot for accommodating resistance. Not confident describing the band anchor and stance precisely from the name alone — the base movement shipped this pass as Close-Grip EZ-Bar Curl.

entries.name: Close-Grip Front Lat Pulldown
entries.reason: Same movement as the shipped Close-Grip Cable Lat Pulldown (close-grip-cable-lat-pulldown) — 'front' just means pulled to the chest rather than behind the neck, which that card already describes.

entries.name: Close-Grip Standing Barbell Curl
entries.reason: Same movement as the shipped Close-Grip Barbell Curl (close-grip-barbell-curl), which is already standing — 'standing' names nothing that card doesn't already do.

entries.name: Crunch - Legs On Exercise Ball
entries.reason: Needs a stability/exercise ball, which has no equipment id in EQUIPMENT — tagging it bodyweight would be the same furniture-mislabeling error the 2026-09-13 review fixed on bench/box cards. Adding a new equipment id is a structural decision beyond a card batch.

entries.name: Crunches
entries.reason: Plain floor crunch, hands by the head — the shipped Crunch (crunch) under a plural title. No distinguishing detail in the reference.

entries.name: Dancer's Stretch
entries.reason: The reference gives name and one muscle (lower back) only. Standing, grabbing the ankle behind you and hinging forward is the same starting shape as the shipped King Dancer Pose (Natarajasana) — not confident whether this names a simpler stretch without the backbend/overhead reach or is the same pose under its dance-studio name, and writing either is a guess.

entries.name: Decline Close-Grip Bench To Skull Crusher
entries.reason: The name implies a hybrid rep that transitions from a close-grip bench press into a skull crusher within one movement, on a decline bench. Not confident of the exact transition point or bar path from the name alone, and it overlaps the shipped Barbell Skull Crusher and EZ-Bar/Dumbbell JM Press family closely enough that a wrong guess at the hybrid detail is worse than skipping it.

entries.name: Double Kettlebell Jerk
entries.reason: No kettlebell jerk of any kind is shipped yet to pattern-match against, and the jerk's dip-drive-catch is exactly the technical-catch class of movement OPERATING.md and the Clean-from-Blocks skip both flag as the hardest part to describe correctly. Not confident enough to write the catch timing from the name alone.

entries.name: Double Kettlebell Snatch
entries.reason: Same technical-catch class the Double Kettlebell Jerk skip already flags: the snatch's bell-rolls-to-lockout catch is the hardest part of the single-arm version to get right (the shipped Kettlebell Snatch card calls it 'powerful and technical'), and doing it with two bells simultaneously doubles the chance of a wrong wrist-rotation detail teaching someone to bang their forearms.

entries.name: Dumbbell Lying Pronation
entries.reason: A real forearm-rotation exercise, but not confident of the exact body position from the name alone -- lying on the back with the working forearm resting across the body, lying on the side, or seated with the forearm on a bench are all plausible readings and the reference gives no instructions to check against. A wrong setup on a small-ROM rotational movement is an easy way to teach the wrong joint action.

entries.name: Dumbbell Lying Supination
entries.reason: Same family and same uncertainty as Dumbbell Lying Pronation -- see that entry.

entries.name: Dumbbell Prone Incline Curl
entries.reason: Duplicate of the already-shipped prone-dumbbell-curl: 'lie face-down on a flat bench raised enough for your arms to hang' is the same body position and the same anti-swing mechanism an incline bench gives this move. Writing a second card for it would ship two entries for one exercise.

entries.name: Dumbbell Seated Box Jump
entries.reason: The name alone doesn't say whether the seated start is on the ground, a low box or the target box, and holding dumbbells through a plyometric landing is a real grip-and-balance risk that a wrongly-guessed setup would only make worse.

entries.name: Dynamic Back Stretch
entries.reason: "Back" covers upper (thoracic rotation/extension) and lower back movement patterns that are not interchangeable, and the name alone does not say which one this is meant to be.

entries.name: Elbows Back
entries.reason: No stable, recognizable movement attaches to this name -- it reads like a cue fragment from a longer routine rather than a named exercise, and guessing a full setup around it risks inventing a stretch that isn't the one meant.

entries.name: EZ-Bar Skullcrusher
entries.reason: Duplicate of the already-shipped ez-bar-skull-crusher: same movement, name differs only by a space and capitalization. Writing a second card would ship two entries for one exercise; the fix is an alias on the shipped card, which is a review-session edit to an existing entry, not a new card.

entries.name: Finger Curls
entries.reason: Its primary target is forearms/grip, and this dataset's MUSCLE_GROUPS enum in exercises.js has no Forearms group -- the nearest existing group is Biceps, which would be a taxonomy call (add a new group, or fold grip work under Biceps) rather than a card-writing one. Leaving it for a review session to decide rather than picking silently.

entries.name: Front Leg Raises
entries.reason: Tagged stretching/hamstrings/bodyweight with no instructions in the reference. The name doesn't say whether it's a standing active raise (using a wall or chair for balance) or a supine/lying raise -- the same body-position ambiguity the Dumbbell Lying Pronation/Supination skips flagged, and picking wrong changes what's actually being stretched.

entries.name: Front Two-Dumbbell Raise
entries.reason: Duplicate of the already-shipped dumbbell-front-raise, whose own description explicitly covers doing it with 'one or both' dumbbells at once. A second card for the two-dumbbell version would duplicate that.

entries.name: Gorilla Chin/Crunch
entries.reason: Not a name with a stable, recognizable technique I could recall confidently, and the reference gives no instructions to check against. Guessing an ab exercise from an unfamiliar name is exactly the recall-error class F10 warns about.

entries.name: Groin and Back Stretch
entries.reason: Too close to the shipped Seated Groin Stretch (fb-seated-groin-stretch) -- a wide-leg seated straddle hinged forward, which stretches both the adductors and the lower back the same way this name implies. Not confident there's a real distinguishing setup (e.g. soles-together butterfly instead of a wide straddle) behind the name rather than a second title for the same stretch.

entries.name: Hang Snatch
entries.reason: An expert-level Olympic barbell lift with a technical catch under the bar. Same class of risk the Double Kettlebell Snatch and Clean from Blocks skips already flag: a wrong catch-timing or bar-path detail teaches an injury, not just a worse rep.

entries.name: Hang Snatch - Below Knees
entries.reason: Same technical-catch Olympic lift as Hang Snatch, starting from a lower hang position -- see that entry.

entries.name: Hanging Bar Good Morning
entries.reason: Not confident what 'hanging' modifies here -- a good morning is normally loaded with the bar racked on the back in a standing hinge, and this name suggests a different, unfamiliar setup the reference gives no detail on. Guessing the rig risks describing a hip hinge that isn't actually how this variation is performed.

entries.name: Hanging Pike
entries.reason: Too close to the already-shipped Hanging Leg Raise (straight legs to horizontal) and Toes-to-Bar (straight legs all the way to the bar) -- both pull-up-bar, straight-leg, hip-flexion moves at Advanced difficulty. A pike differs mainly by a posterior pelvic tilt cue at the top, which reads as a form refinement on the same movement rather than a distinct exercise, and this record's own 'expert' tag (one step past the shipped Advanced card) supports that reading.

entries.name: Heaving Snatch Balance
entries.reason: An Olympic lifting drill built around dropping under the bar and catching it in an overhead squat -- the same technical-catch class of movement the Hang Snatch and Double Kettlebell Snatch skips flag. Not confident of the exact drop timing and receiving position from the name alone.

entries.name: Hyperextensions With No Hyperextension Bench
entries.reason: Duplicate of the already-shipped Bodyweight Back Extension (bodyweight-back-extension) -- lying face-down and lifting the chest with the lower back is exactly the floor variant this name describes, and that card already carries the alias 'Floor Back Extension'.

entries.name: Incline Dumbbell Flyes
entries.reason: Duplicate of the already-shipped Incline Dumbbell Fly (dumbbell-incline-fly), differing only by pluralization. The fix is an alias on the existing card, which is a review-session edit, not a new one.

entries.name: Incline Inner Biceps Curl
entries.reason: Not confident of the exact detail that separates it from a plain Incline Dumbbell Curl -- memory of this variant conflicts between 'arms hang out to the sides for a longer stretch' and 'curl in toward the center of the body,' and the reference gives no instructions to check against. Guessing which is wrong is the recall-error class F10 warns about.

entries.name: Incline Dumbbell Bench With Palms Facing In
entries.reason: Written as Neutral-Grip Incline Dumbbell Press, then dropped after pending.mjs BLOCKed it as a duplicate of the shipped Incline Dumbbell Bench Press (via its own alias 'Incline Dumbbell Press'). It is a real, distinct grip variant, not a duplicate -- the containment check has no discriminating word for 'neutral'/'grip', so any incline+dumbbell+press name collapses onto the plain press. See bellows/FINDINGS.md for the checker gap. Left out rather than shipped past a BLOCK.

entries.name: Incline Dumbbell Flyes - With A Twist
entries.reason: Written as Incline Dumbbell Fly with a Twist, then dropped after pending.mjs BLOCKed it as a duplicate of the shipped Incline Dumbbell Fly (via its own alias). Same containment-check gap as the neutral-grip press skip above: 'twist' is not a discriminating word, so the shorter existing name is fully contained and the check calls it covered. See bellows/FINDINGS.md.

entries.name: Isometric Neck Exercise - Front And Back
entries.reason: isCovered() returns false (no lexical overlap with the existing name), but this is the same movement already shipped as Neck Isometric Holds (fb-neck-isometric): press the head into a palm on the forehead and again on the back of the head, holding without moving. Writing it under a new name would be a real duplicate the checker cannot see, not a gap.

entries.name: Isometric Neck Exercise - Sides
entries.reason: Same movement as fb-neck-isometric (Neck Isometric Holds), which already covers pressing the head into a palm on each side -- its own description says 'and on each side.' Same undetected-duplicate shape as the front-and-back entry above.

entries.name: Isometric Wipers
entries.reason: Not confident of the exact movement. The reference lists this as chest-targeted, which does not match any known 'windshield wiper' exercise (normally a hanging or floor ab/oblique movement); the isometric-hold variant's body position, arm placement and which direction is held are not something I can reconstruct correctly from the name alone. Recall-error class F10 warns about.

entries.name: Kettlebell Pass Between The Legs
entries.reason: isCovered() returns false (no lexical overlap with the existing name), but this is the same movement already shipped as Kettlebell Figure Eight: its own description is 'pass the kettlebell between your legs from one hand to the other, weaving it around each leg in a figure-eight pattern.' Writing it under this name would be a real duplicate the checker cannot see, not a gap -- same F14-class vocabulary gap as the neck entries above.

entries.name: Leverage Chest Press
entries.reason: ExRx describes this as the plain, wide-overhand-grip lever chest press where both handles move together -- the shipped 'Machine Chest Press' (id machine-chest-press) is that same generic synchronized chest press machine, just named by equipment category rather than the ExRx 'Lever' family name. isCovered() returns false because 'Leverage'/'Lever' and 'Machine' share no words, but the two names point at the same real machine. Not the same as the already-shipped 'Hammer Strength Chest Press', which is explicitly the independent-arm (isolateral) variant.

entries.name: Leverage Incline Chest Press
entries.reason: Same gap as 'Leverage Chest Press' one entry up: ExRx's plain 'Lever Incline Chest Press' (wide overhand grip, both handles move together) is the same machine as the shipped 'Incline Machine Chest Press' (id incline-machine-chest-press), just under the equipment-generic name instead of the ExRx 'Lever' name. No independent-arm incline press is shipped, so if this checker gap is ever fixed, an isolateral incline variant would still be a real, writable gap -- this specific plain version is not.

entries.name: Leverage Shoulder Press
entries.reason: Same 'Lever'-vs-'Machine' naming gap, third instance today. ExRx's plain Lever Shoulder Press is 'press lever upward until arms are extended overhead' -- a seated, both-handles-together press, mechanically identical to the already-shipped 'Machine Shoulder Press' (id machine-shoulder-press: 'sit ... grip the handles at shoulder height. Press up until your arms are nearly straight'). isCovered() returns false because 'Leverage'/'Lever' and 'Machine' share no words. ExRx does list a separate isolateral ('Lever Isolateral Shoulder Press, plate loaded') variant, which is not shipped and would be a real gap if named explicitly.

entries.name: Leverage Iso Row
entries.reason: 'Iso' here means isolateral (independent-arm) -- a chest-supported, plate-loaded row where each handle moves on its own, pulled to the chest. That is exactly the already-shipped 'Hammer Strength Row' (id hammer-strength-row: 'chest on the pad ... row them back ... each arm works on its own, so a weaker side can't hide'). Same equipment-name-vs-brand-name gap as the chest presses above, just for a row.

entries.name: Lower Back Curl
entries.reason: Two independent sources (Aspira Fitness and Ellim.app, checked by web search since the vendored reference carries no instructions) agree it is: lie face-down, arms extended overhead, lift arms/chest/legs off the floor together, hold, lower. That is the already-shipped 'Superman' (id superman: 'Lie face-down with your arms stretched out in front. Squeeze your lower back and glutes to lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor at the same time'). Same movement under a different name; isCovered() misses it because the two names share no words.

entries.name: Lunge Sprint
entries.reason: free-exercise-db tags this equipment=machine, target=quadriceps, which sounded suspicious for a name like 'Lunge Sprint' -- checked by web search rather than trusted blind. The only match for that machine/quads combination (a Smith-machine bar-on-back alternating jump lunge) came from a site that mirrors the dataset's own field names, not an independent source, plus one weak Pinterest listing title. Two unrelated, much more common exercises share confusingly similar names: 'Sprinter Lunge' (bodyweight, sprinter's-arm-swing drill, unanimous across StrengthLog/PureGym/Trainwell) and 'Smith Sprint Lunge' (a rear-foot-elevated split squat, no jump). Not confident enough to write an accurate how-to; a wrong description here teaches the wrong movement.

entries.name: Lying Glute
entries.reason: Checked by web search (ExRx, LoadMuscle, Kovo Fitness and others agree, since the vendored reference carries no instructions): lie on your back, knees bent, cross one ankle over the opposite knee into a figure-4, then pull the supporting thigh toward your chest. That is the already-shipped 'Supine Figure-4 Glute Stretch' (id fb-figure-four-glute: 'cross one ankle over the opposite thigh just above the knee, then reach through the gap and pull the supporting thigh toward your chest'). Same movement under a different name; isCovered() misses it because the two names share no words -- same shape as the 'Lower Back Curl'/'Superman' skip above.

entries.name: Lying One-Arm Lateral Raise
entries.reason: Checked by web search since the vendored reference carries no instructions: every independent source found (Jefit, fitloop.app, atletiq, liftmanual) that uses this exact name describes the posterior-deltoid movement -- chest down on a bench, one dumbbell raised out to the side with the shoulder blade squeezed back -- not a side-delt raise. That is the already-shipped 'Dumbbell Lying One-Arm Rear Lateral Raise' (id dumbbell-lying-one-arm-rear-lateral-raise: 'Lie chest-down on an incline bench holding a dumbbell in one hand ... raise the dumbbell out to your side ... squeezing that shoulder blade back'). Same movement; free-exercise-db's name drops the word 'Rear' and isCovered() misses it because the two names then share no discriminating word -- same shape as the 'Lying Glute' skip above.

entries.name: Iron Crosses (stretch)
entries.reason: Checked by web search since the vendored reference carries no instructions (and equipment=null, remapped to bodyweight): sportsfitnesshut, strive-workout, grabgains, gymbrah and liftmanual all describe the same lying spinal-twist movement -- on your back, arms out in a T, cross one leg over the other and let both knees drop toward the floor on that side. That is the already-shipped 'Lying Crossover Stretch' (id lying-crossover-stretch: 'Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, and arms out to the sides in a T. Cross one knee over the other, then let both knees fall together toward the floor'). Same movement under the gymnast-shape nickname; isCovered() misses it because 'Crosses' stems to a form that doesn't match 'Crossover' and the two names share no other word.

entries.name: Looking At Ceiling
entries.reason: Checked by web search since the vendored reference carries no instructions: atletiq and fitwill agree it is kneel, hold both heels, lift the hips forward and arch back to look at the ceiling. That is the already-shipped yoga 'Camel Pose' / Ustrasana (id yoga-camel: 'Kneel with your knees hip-width and your hands on your lower back, fingers pointing down. Press your hips forward and lift your chest toward the ceiling, reaching for your heels'). Same posture under its plain-English name instead of its yoga one; isCovered() misses it because 'Looking At Ceiling' and 'Camel Pose'/'Ustrasana' share no word at all.

entries.name: Lying Prone Quadriceps
entries.reason: Checked by web search since the vendored reference carries no instructions: ExRx, nismat.org, stretching.wonderhowto.com and inspireusafoundation agree it is lie face down, bend one knee, reach back and pull the ankle toward your backside while both hip bones stay on the floor. That is the already-shipped 'Prone Quad Stretch' (id static-prone-quad: 'Lie face down, bend one knee and reach back for the ankle ... Draw the heel toward your backside while keeping both hip bones on the floor'), almost word for word. isCovered() misses it because 'Quadriceps' doesn't stem to match 'Quad' and the two names then share no word.

entries.name: Lying Rear Delt Raise
entries.reason: Checked by web search since the vendored reference carries no instructions: Fittr and FitnessVolt both describe lying chest-down on an incline bench, a dumbbell in each hand, raising both out to the sides until level with the torso. That is the already-shipped 'Dumbbell Lying Rear Lateral Raise' (id dumbbell-lying-rear-lateral-raise: 'Lie chest-down on an incline bench holding a dumbbell in each hand ... Raise both dumbbells out to your sides until your arms are level with your torso'). Same bilateral movement as the already-skipped one-arm version (2026-10-01 morning); free-exercise-db's name drops 'Lateral' and isCovered() misses it because the two names share no discriminating word.

entries.name: Lying Triceps Press
entries.reason: Checked by web search since the vendored reference carries no instructions: muscleandstrength and bodybuilding-wizard both describe lying on a flat bench holding an EZ-bar on its INNER angle (close grip), lowering it beyond the forehead and pressing back up -- the classic skull-crusher. That is the already-shipped 'Lying Close-Grip EZ-Bar Triceps Press To Chin', same equipment, same inner-grip, same bar path. free-exercise-db's generic name drops 'close-grip' and 'to chin' and isCovered() misses it because those are the only discriminating words.

entries.name: Machine Bench Press
entries.reason: A direct name match this time, not a web-search one: the shipped 'Machine Chest Press' (id machine-chest-press) is 'Sit in the chest press machine with the handles at chest height and your back flat against the pad. Press the handles forward until your arms are nearly straight' -- the identical seated flat press this queue item's own sourcing (jefit, sweat.com) describes. isCovered() misses it because 'bench' and 'chest' share no word, the same shape as the F14 skips already on this list.

entries.name: Middle Back Stretch
entries.reason: Checked by web search since the vendored reference carries no instructions: the only independent description found (ellim.app) is seated, knee crossed or hand on the opposite thigh, rotating the torso -- the already-shipped 'Seated Spinal Twist' (id yoga-seated-spinal-twist, aliases Ardha Matsyendrasana / Half Lord of the Fishes): 'Sit with your legs out, bend the right knee and cross it over the left thigh ... turn a little further as you breathe out.' isCovered() misses it because the two names share no word at all.

entries.name: Moving Claw Series
entries.reason: No independent how-to found. The only two results (myworkouts.io, atletiq) restate the vendored free-exercise-db metadata (bodyweight, glutes/hamstrings, plyometric, intermediate) with no description of the actual movement -- the same 'name alone, no instructions' shape F10 already warns against. Dropping rather than guessing at what a 'claw' drill does with the hamstrings.

entries.name: Oblique Crunches
entries.reason: Two independent sources (hevyapp, thegymgroup) describe lying on the back with knees bent and feet flat, elbow brought to the opposite knee in an alternating twist -- the identical movement already shipped as 'Cross-Body Crunch' (id cross-body-crunch): 'Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat ... that elbow travels toward the opposite knee as that knee draws in to meet it ... alternate sides.' Not the same as the already-shipped 'Side Crunch' (alias 'Oblique Crunch', singular), which drops both knees to one side instead of alternating.

entries.name: Olympic Squat
entries.reason: Independent sources (fitbod, liftmanual) describe it as 'a variation of the standard Back Squat' with a more upright torso and a slightly wider, angled-out stance -- a bar-position and torso-angle emphasis on the same movement already shipped as 'Barbell Back Squat' (id barbell-back-squat), which specifies no particular bar height or torso angle itself. Unlike this pass's Narrow Stance Squat (a clearly narrower stance with a named, sourced difference in muscle emphasis), the distinguishing detail here was too subtle to confidently describe as a separate card rather than restating the same squat.

entries.name: Narrow Stance Hack Squats
entries.reason: A real, sourced variant (muscleandstrength, jefit, gymwolf all describe the narrow foot placement and its shift toward the outer quads), written as 'Narrow Stance Hack Squat Machine' and then BLOCKed by pending.mjs as a duplicate of the already-shipped 'Hack Squat Machine' -- neither 'narrow' nor 'stance' is in coverage.mjs's DISCRIMINATING list, so the shorter shipped name (once 'machine' is counted) reads as fully contained. Same F14 shape as the Incline Dumbbell neutral-grip/twist skips from 2026-09-23: dropped rather than shipped past the gate. Real and writable if DISCRIMINATING ever learns 'narrow'/'stance'.

entries.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Clean
entries.reason: The already-shipped 'Kettlebell Clean' (id kettlebell-clean-conditioning) is already a single-bell, one-arm lift -- unilateral: true, 'Hike the kettlebell back ... pull it up to the rack position on your shoulder' -- which is what a kettlebell clean means by default; the two-bell version is the already-shipped, separately-named 'Double Kettlebell Clean'. 'One-Arm' here just restates the shipped card. isCovered() reads it as uncovered because 'arm' is a DISCRIMINATING word the shipped name doesn't carry -- the F14 shape running in the other direction, a false 'new' reading on a true duplicate.

entries.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Snatch
entries.reason: Same shape as this pass's One-Arm Kettlebell Clean: the already-shipped 'Kettlebell Snatch' (id kettlebell-snatch-conditioning) is already unilateral: true and describes swinging and punching a single bell overhead in one motion -- a kettlebell snatch is a one-bell lift by definition, and no 'Double Kettlebell Snatch' is shipped to make 'One-Arm' a meaningful disambiguation. 'One-Arm' and 'Snatch' restate the shipped card rather than adding anything.

entries.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Military Press To The Side
entries.reason: Sourced (jefit, fitwill, lyfta): a standing strict press from the rack position, pressed in a slight arc to clear the face and lock out over the shoulder, torso held still throughout -- the same setup, path and finish as the already-shipped 'Single-Arm Kettlebell Press' (id single-arm-kettlebell-press): 'Hold a kettlebell at one shoulder ... press it overhead ... while keeping your body from leaning.' The arc 'to the side' to clear the face is ordinary technique for any one-arm kettlebell press, not a distinct movement -- 'military' and 'side' are DISCRIMINATING words with no match on the shipped name, not evidence of a real variant.

entries.name: One Half Locust
entries.reason: A real, sourced variant (yogabasics, yogapedia, tummee all describe Ardha Shalabhasana as lifting one straight leg at a time instead of both), written as 'Half Locust Pose' and then BLOCKed by pending.mjs as a duplicate of the already-shipped 'Locust Pose' -- 'half' is not in coverage.mjs's DISCRIMINATING list, so the shorter shipped name reads as fully contained once it is ignored. Same F14 shape as the Narrow Stance Hack Squat skip earlier this stack: dropped rather than shipped past the gate. Real and writable if DISCRIMINATING ever learns 'half'.

entries.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Clean and Jerk
entries.reason: A real, sourced, technically distinct lift (barbend, strongfirst, kettlebellkings: the jerk's re-dip catch under the bell vs the press's single continuous lockout), written as 'Kettlebell Clean and Jerk' and then BLOCKed by pending.mjs as a duplicate of the already-shipped 'Kettlebell Clean' -- 'jerk' is not in coverage.mjs's DISCRIMINATING list, so 'kettlebell' + 'clean' alone read as fully containing the shipped two-word name. The standalone 'Kettlebell Jerk' (no clean) shipped this same pass without tripping the check. Dropped rather than shipped past the gate; real and writable if DISCRIMINATING ever learns 'jerk'.

entries.name: Open Palm Kettlebell Clean
entries.reason: Written, then checked by hand rather than trusted on a clean isCovered() read: it is a coaching drill for the already-shipped 'Kettlebell Clean' (id kettlebell-clean-conditioning), not a different exercise -- the open-palm cue teaches the same hip-drive clean without changing the movement's purpose, load, or muscles worked. isCovered() read it as uncovered because 'open' and 'palm' are not DISCRIMINATING words, which is the F14 shape running in the duplicate direction. Dropped rather than shipped past the gate.

entries.name: One-Arm Long Bar Row
entries.reason: Written, then found by hand to be the already-shipped 'One-Arm Landmine Row' (id barbell-landmine-one-arm-row) under a name almost identical to its own alias 'Bent Over One-Arm Long Bar Row' -- same setup (wedge one end of a barbell in a corner, straddle it, row the free end one-handed), same equipment, same pattern. isCovered() did not flag it because 'landmine' and 'long'/'bar' share no word, so the automated check never compared the new title against the shipped alias meaningfully despite them being four of five words identical. Dropped rather than shipped past the gate; the shipped card's alias list already covers this title closely enough that coverage.mjs should not re-queue it, but if it does, do not ship it again.

entries.name: Side Lateral Raise
entries.reason: Written as 'One-Arm Dumbbell Lateral Raise' (equipment resolved to dumbbell) and BLOCKed by pending.mjs as a duplicate of the already-shipped 'Dumbbell Lateral Raise'. Checked by hand: the shipped card is two-handed but the biomechanics of raising one dumbbell out to the side are identical whether or not the other arm moves at the same time -- unlike the kettlebell one-arm variants this stack has shipped (swing, overhead squat), nothing about grip, path, or stabilizer demand changes by doing one side at a time. Not a distinct exercise; dropped rather than shipped past the gate.

entries.name: Rear Leg Raises
entries.reason: Researched before writing (the vendored reference carries no instructions): free-exercise-db describes it as hands-and-knees, extending one leg straight back with both knee and hip extending to hip height. That is the already-shipped 'Quadruped Hip Extension' (id quadruped-hip-extension) movement verbatim -- isCovered() missed it because the two names share zero words, not because the movements differ. Dropped rather than shipped past the gate.

entries.name: Return Push from Stance
entries.reason: The vendored reference carries only a name and equipment tag, no instructions (medicine ball, plyometrics, shoulders, beginner). A targeted search found no independent source describing this exact named drill precisely enough to be confident of the technique -- the nearest hits ('Medicine Ball Chest Push from Stance', 'Medicine Ball Chest Push From 3 Point Stance') may or may not be the same movement under a shortened name. Per the standing rule, a missing card is recoverable and a wrong one is not -- skipped rather than guessed.

entries.name: Reverse Band Bench Press
entries.reason: Confirmed via powerliftingtechnique.com and elitefts: reverse band work requires heavy bands choked around the top of a power rack (or a monolift) to pull the bar upward, giving more assistance at the bottom of the lift and less at the top -- the opposite effect of the shipped 'Resistance Band Squat', which loops a band under the feet for MORE resistance at the top. This app's 15-item equipment list has no entry for a rack or band-anchor rig, and tagging it barbell+resistance-band would misrepresent the setup as 'add a normal band', which it is not. Skipped for an equipment-taxonomy mismatch, not a duplicate.
